docs.title: Vllama 🦙
docs.text:
One CLI for everything AI — locally or on free cloud GPUs.

Image generation · AutoML · Local LLMs · Speech · Object Detection · 3D · VS Code

pip install vllama

Get Started View on GitHub

docs.title: What is Vllama?
docs.text:
Vllama is a single CLI tool that puts state-of-the-art AI at your fingertips — without needing a powerful GPU or writing any code.

No GPU? No problem.

Vllama can offload heavy models like Stable Diffusion to Kaggle's free GPU and automatically download the results to your machine. All you need is a Kaggle account.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
🎨

Image Generation

Run Stable Diffusion and other diffusion models locally or on Kaggle GPUs.

🤖

Local LLMs

Spin up any HuggingFace chat model as a local REST API server in one command.

🆚

VS Code Extension

Chat with your locally running LLM directly inside VS Code's native chat panel — zero API keys.

📷

Object Detection

Run YOLO on images and videos from the terminal instantly.

🎬

Video Generation

Generate videos from text prompts using text-to-video models.

🔊

Speech

Text-to-speech and speech-to-text using local models — no cloud API needed.

🖼️

Image/Video to 3D

Generate 3D .ply models from images or videos via Kaggle GPU.

🏆

AutoML

Preprocess any CSV and auto-train 9+ ML models with hyperparameter tuning in two commands.

docs.title: 5-Minute Examples
docs.text:
Image GenerationAutoMLLocal LLMObject Detection 
# Login to Kaggle once (free account)
vllama login --service kaggle --username YOU --key YOUR_KEY

# Generate an image on free Kaggle GPU
vllama run stabilityai/sd-turbo --service kaggle --prompt "A cyberpunk city at night"

# Step 1: Preprocess your CSV
vllama data --path housing.csv --target price

# Step 2: Train 9 models and get a leaderboard
vllama train --path ./output_folder_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS --target price

# Terminal 1: Start local LLM server
vllama run_llm Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct

# Terminal 2: Chat with it
vllama chat_llm

# Detect objects in a photo
vllama detect_image --path photo.jpg

# Detect objects in a video
vllama detect_video --path video.mp4

docs.title: General
docs.text:
What is Vllama?

Vllama is a CLI tool that lets you run AI models locally — or offload them to free Kaggle GPUs — from your terminal. It covers image generation, AutoML, local LLMs, object detection, speech, 3D, and more.

Do I need a GPU?

No. Vllama runs on CPU and automatically falls back gracefully. For heavy models like Stable Diffusion, use --service kaggle to run on Kaggle's free T4 GPU instead.

Is it free?

Yes. Vllama is open source (Apache 2.0). Kaggle GPU offload uses Kaggle's free tier (~30 GPU hours/week).

What Python versions are supported?

Python 3.8 and above.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install vllama fails with a dependency error

Try upgrading pip first:

pip install --upgrade pip
pip install vllama

If a specific package fails, check if you need system-level dependencies (e.g., portaudio for speech features on macOS/Linux).

Can I install just part of Vllama?

Currently pip install vllama installs the full package. Heavy dependencies (PyTorch, Diffusers, etc.) are imported lazily and only download model weights when you first use a feature.

docs.title: Kaggle GPU
docs.text:
How do I get my Kaggle API key?

Log in at kaggle.com → Settings → API → Create New Token. This downloads kaggle.json containing your username and key.

My Kaggle GPU quota is exceeded

Kaggle gives ~30 GPU hours per week for free accounts. Quota resets weekly. Check your usage at kaggle.com/account.

The Kaggle run is stuck / never downloads

Check the Kaggle kernel status at kaggle.com/code. If the kernel errored, check its output logs for the error message.

docs.title: Image Generation
docs.text:
Generation is slow on CPU

This is expected. Diffusion models are designed for GPUs. Use --service kaggle to run on a free Kaggle GPU, or use stabilityai/sd-turbo which is specifically optimized for speed.

"CUDA out of memory"

Vllama automatically falls back to CPU or uses memory-efficient settings for low-VRAM GPUs. If you still get OOM, try --service kaggle.

docs.title: Local LLMs
docs.text:
"VS Code extension can't connect to local LLM"

Make sure vllama run_llm <model> is running and shows Running on http://localhost:2513 before opening VS Code chat. Check extension settings for the correct port.

Model downloads are slow

HuggingFace models download from the internet the first time. A 7B model is 10–14GB. Subsequent runs use the local cache at ~/.cache/huggingface.

docs.title: Speech
docs.text:
"No microphone found" when running vllama stt

Make sure your system has a working microphone and audio drivers. On Linux, also install: sudo apt-get install portaudio19-dev.

vllama stt requires internet?

Yes, the STT command uses Google Speech Recognition which sends audio to Google's API. The TTS and translation commands (vllama tts, vllama translate) run fully offline.

docs.title: AutoML
docs.text:
"Target column not found"

Specify the column name explicitly:

vllama data --path data.csv --target your_actual_column_name

Use head data.csv or python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.read_csv('data.csv').columns.tolist())" to check your column names.

Training takes very long

Large datasets with hyperparameter search take longer. For faster testing, subsample your data first. Training time scales with dataset size × number of models.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher
  • pip

That's all you need to get started. Heavy dependencies like PyTorch and Diffusers are pulled in on first use, not at install time.

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
pip install vllama

Verify the install:

vllama --help

docs.title: System-specific Notes
docs.text:
WindowsmacOSLinux

Install works normally on Windows. For Speech commands (vllama stt), you may need to install PortAudio:

pip install pipwin
pipwin install pyaudio

PortAudio is required for speech features:

brew install portaudio
pip install vllama

sudo apt-get install portaudio19-dev  # for speech features
pip install vllama

docs.title: Virtual Environment (Recommended)
docs.text:
Running in a virtual environment keeps your global Python clean:

python -m venv vllama-env

# Activate
source vllama-env/bin/activate   # Linux / macOS
vllama-env\Scripts\activate      # Windows

pip install vllama

docs.title: GPU Support (Optional but Faster)
docs.text:
Vllama works on CPU out of the box. For GPU acceleration, install PyTorch with CUDA support before installing vllama:

# CUDA 11.8
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118

# CUDA 12.1
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121

# Then install vllama
pip install vllama

No GPU locally?

Use Vllama's built-in Kaggle GPU offload to run heavy models for free without any local GPU.

docs.title: VS Code Extension
docs.text:
To use the VS Code chat integration:

  1. Open VS Code
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+X (or Cmd+Shift+X on macOS)
  3. Search for Vllama
  4. Click Install

The extension connects to a local LLM server you start with vllama run_llm. See the Local LLM in VS Code guide.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text: pip install --upgrade vllama

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
pip uninstall vllama

Model weights cached by HuggingFace are stored in ~/.cache/huggingface. Remove that directory to free disk space.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Five working examples to get you productive in under five minutes.

docs.title: 1. Generate an Image (No GPU Needed)
docs.text:
If you have a Kaggle account (free), you can offload image generation to their GPU:

# One-time setup: connect your Kaggle account
vllama login --service kaggle --username YOUR_USERNAME --key YOUR_API_KEY

# Generate an image — runs on Kaggle's free T4 GPU, downloads to your machine
vllama run stabilityai/sd-turbo --service kaggle --prompt "A neon-lit city street at night"

The image is saved as vllama_kaggle_<timestamp>.png in your current directory.

Where to find your Kaggle API key

Go to kaggle.com → Account → API → Create New Token. This downloads kaggle.json. Your username and key are in that file.

docs.title: 2. AutoML: Train Models on Your CSV
docs.text:
Two commands to go from a raw CSV to a trained model leaderboard:

# Step 1: Preprocess your dataset
vllama data --path my_data.csv --target target_column

# Step 2: Train all models on the preprocessed data
# (replace the folder name with the one created in Step 1)
vllama train --path ./output_folder_20240101_120000 --target target_column

After vllama train, open results/report.html in your browser for a full interactive leaderboard.

Don't have a dataset handy? Grab the Titanic dataset:

# Download the Titanic dataset
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datasciencedojo/datasets/master/titanic.csv

vllama data --path titanic.csv --target Survived
vllama train --path ./output_folder_* --target Survived

docs.title: 3. Run a Local LLM and Chat With It
docs.text:
# Terminal 1: Start a local LLM server (downloads model on first run)
vllama run_llm Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct

# Terminal 2: Chat with it
vllama chat_llm

You> Write a Python function to reverse a linked list
Assistant> Here's a function...

The model runs entirely on your machine. No internet after the initial download, no API keys, no usage costs.

docs.title: 4. Detect Objects in an Image
docs.text:
# From a local file
vllama detect_image --path photo.jpg

# From a URL
vllama detect_image --url https://ultralytics.com/images/bus.jpg

Results are saved to the current directory with bounding boxes drawn on the image.

docs.title: 5. Text-to-Speech
docs.text:
# Speak text directly
vllama tts --text "Hello from Vllama"

# Interactive mode — enter multiple lines
vllama tts

docs.text: All Vllama commands, organised by category.

docs.title: Global Flags
docs.text:
These flags work across all commands:

Flag Description --help Show help for the command --version Show the installed Vllama version

docs.title: Cloud & GPU Commands
docs.text: Vllama integrates with Kaggle to let you offload compute-heavy tasks to their free GPU — no payment required, just a Kaggle account.

docs.title: vllama login — Authenticate with Kaggle
docs.text: Save your Kaggle credentials so Vllama can submit kernels on your behalf.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama login --service kaggle [--username <user>] [--key <api_key>]

docs.title: How to Get Your Kaggle API Key
docs.text:
1. Go to kaggle.com and log in
  2. Click your profile picture → Settings
  3. Scroll to API section → Create New Token
  4. A kaggle.json file downloads containing your username and key

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Provide credentials directly
vllama login --service kaggle --username manvith --key abcdef1234567890

# Use existing kaggle.json at ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json
vllama login --service kaggle

docs.title: vllama logout — Remove Credentials
docs.text:
vllama logout

Removes saved Kaggle credentials from your machine.

docs.title: vllama init gpu — Initialize a GPU Session
docs.text:
Prepares a GPU-enabled Kaggle kernel for use.

vllama init gpu --service kaggle

This is typically called automatically when you run commands with --service kaggle. You can run it manually to verify connectivity.

docs.title: Using Kaggle GPU with Any Command
docs.text:
Add --service kaggle to these commands to offload to Kaggle's free T4 GPU:

# Image generation on Kaggle GPU
vllama run stabilityai/sd-turbo --service kaggle --prompt "..."

# Video generation on Kaggle GPU
vllama run_video damo-vilab/text-to-video-ms-1.7b --service kaggle --prompt "..."

# Image to 3D on Kaggle GPU
vllama image3d --path photo.jpg --service kaggle

# Video to 3D on Kaggle GPU
vllama video3d --path clip.mp4 --service kaggle

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When you add --service kaggle:

  1. Vllama creates a Kaggle notebook kernel via the Kaggle API
  2. The kernel runs with a free T4 GPU enabled
  3. Vllama installs the required dependencies inside the kernel
  4. The model runs and generates the output
  5. The output file is downloaded to your local machine automatically

Kaggle GPU limits

Kaggle provides approximately 30 GPU hours per week for free accounts. Each image generation takes a few minutes.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Alternatively, set credentials as environment variables instead of using vllama login:

export KAGGLE_USERNAME=your_username
export KAGGLE_KEY=your_api_key

Or create a .env file in your project directory:

KAGGLE_USERNAME=your_username
KAGGLE_KEY=your_api_key
HF_HOME=/path/to/model/cache        # optional: custom model cache dir
HF_TOKEN=your_huggingface_token     # optional: for gated models like Llama 2

For a detailed step-by-step walkthrough, see the No GPU Guide.

docs.title: vllama data — Data Preprocessing
docs.text: Automatically cleans, encodes, scales, and splits any tabular dataset, and generates visualizations of the data.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama data --path <dataset> [--target <column>] [--test_size <float>] [--output_dir <dir>]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Short Default Description --path required Path to dataset file --target auto-detect Name of the target column --test_size -t 0.2 Fraction of data to hold out for testing --output_dir -o current dir Where to save output files

Supported input formats: CSV, Excel (.xlsx), JSON, Parquet.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
When you run vllama data, it performs the following steps automatically:

  1. Loads and inspects the dataset — shape, dtypes, missing value rates
  2. Removes duplicates and rows with excessive missing data
  3. Handles missing values — KNN imputation for numerics, mode filling for categoricals
  4. Handles outliers — detects and caps extreme values using IQR
  5. Encodes categoricals — label encoding, one-hot encoding, or frequency encoding based on cardinality
  6. Scales numeric features using RobustScaler (outlier-resistant)
  7. Feature selection — removes zero-variance and highly correlated (>0.95) features
  8. Splits into train / test sets
  9. Generates visualizations — missing values heatmap, correlation matrix, target distribution, mutual information scores

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Minimal — auto-detect target column
vllama data --path sales_data.csv

# Specify target column and 25% test split
vllama data --path housing.csv --target price --test_size 0.25

# Custom output directory
vllama data --path data.csv --target label -t 0.3 -o ./processed

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text:
All outputs go into a timestamped folder:

output_folder_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS/
├── train_data.csv              ← Training set (80% by default)
├── test_data.csv               ← Test set (20% by default)
├── processed_full_data.csv     ← Full preprocessed dataset
├── preprocessing_log.json      ← Detailed JSON log of every step
├── preprocessing_log.txt       ← Human-readable log
├── summary_report.json         ← Summary statistics
├── transformation_metadata.json  ← Encoders & scalers (for inference later)
└── visualizations/
    ├── 01_missing_initial.png
    ├── 02_dtypes.png
    ├── 03_corr_processed.png
    ├── 04_target_processed.png
    └── 05_mi.png

Save the folder name

The timestamped output folder is what you pass to vllama train. Copy it after vllama data finishes.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text:
Pass the output folder to vllama train to automatically train and compare ML models on your preprocessed data.

vllama train --path ./output_folder_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS --target price

docs.title: vllama detect_image — Detect Objects in an Image
docs.text: Run YOLO object detection on a single image.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama detect_image [--path <image>] [--url <url>] [--model <yolo>] [--output_dir <dir>]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Short Default Description --path Path to a local image file --url URL of an image to fetch and detect --model -m yolov8n.pt YOLO model variant --output_dir -o current dir Where to save the annotated output

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Local file
vllama detect_image --path photo.jpg

# From URL
vllama detect_image --url https://ultralytics.com/images/bus.jpg

# Use a larger, more accurate model
vllama detect_image --path photo.jpg --model yolov8s.pt

# Custom output directory
vllama detect_image --path photo.jpg -o ./detections

docs.title: YOLO Model Variants
docs.text: Model Size Speed Accuracy yolov8n.pt Nano Fastest Lower yolov8s.pt Small Fast Medium yolov8m.pt Medium Moderate Good yolov8l.pt Large Slower High yolov8x.pt XLarge Slowest Highest

docs.title: vllama detect_video — Detect Objects in a Video
docs.text: Run YOLO object detection frame-by-frame on a video file.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama detect_video --path <video> [--model <yolo>] [--output_dir <dir>]

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
vllama detect_video --path video.mp4 -o ./outputs
vllama detect_video --path clip.mp4 --model yolov8s.pt

Output is an annotated video file saved in the output directory.

docs.title: vllama image3d — Image to 3D Model
docs.text: Generate a 3D .ply model from a single image using Kaggle GPU.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama image3d [--path <image>] [--url <url>] [--service kaggle] [--output_dir <dir>]

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
vllama image3d --path object_photo.jpg --service kaggle -o ./3d_outputs
vllama image3d --url https://example.com/object.jpg --service kaggle

Kaggle required

image3d runs on Kaggle's GPU. Make sure you are logged in with vllama login --service kaggle.

docs.title: vllama video3d — Video to 3D Model
docs.text: Generate a 3D .ply model from a video file using Kaggle GPU.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama video3d --path <video> [--service kaggle] [--output_dir <dir>] [--frame_interval <n>]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Short Default Description --path required Path to input video --service -s Cloud service (kaggle) --output_dir -o current dir Where to save output --frame_interval -f 5 Process every Nth frame

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
vllama video3d --path object_scan.mp4 --service kaggle -o ./3d_outputs
vllama video3d --path scan.mp4 --service kaggle -f 10

docs.title: View the Output
docs.text:
After generating a .ply file, use vllama view3d to open it in an interactive 3D viewer.

vllama view3d --path output.ply

docs.title: Local LLM Commands
docs.text: Run any HuggingFace chat model as a local REST API and chat with it — no API keys, no internet after the first download, no usage costs.

docs.title: vllama run_llm — Start a Local LLM Server
docs.text: Downloads and starts any HuggingFace chat model as a REST API server on localhost:2513.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama run_llm <model_name>

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Qwen Coder (small, fast, great for code)
vllama run_llm Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct

# Llama 2 Chat (requires HuggingFace token for gated access)
vllama run_llm meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf

# Microsoft DialoGPT
vllama run_llm microsoft/DialoGPT-medium

docs.title: What Starts Up
docs.text:
Once running, the server:

  • Listens on http://localhost:2513
  • Exposes a /chat endpoint
  • Maintains conversation history across turns
  • Works with vllama chat_llm and the VS Code extension

docs.title: API Endpoint
docs.text:
You can also talk to the server directly via HTTP:

curl -X POST http://localhost:2513/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Write a Python function to sort a list"}'

Response:

{
  "response": "Here's a Python function..."
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The server runs in the foreground. Press Ctrl+C to stop it.
  • Models are cached in ~/.cache/huggingface after first download.
  • Gated models (like Llama 2) require a HuggingFace token: set HF_TOKEN=your_token in your environment.

docs.title: vllama chat_llm — CLI Chat
docs.text: Connect to a running LLM server and chat interactively in the terminal.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama chat_llm

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
First, start the server in one terminal:

# Terminal 1
vllama run_llm Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct

Then chat in another:

# Terminal 2
vllama chat_llm

You> What is a closure in Python?
Assistant> A closure is a function that remembers the values from its enclosing scope...

You> Give me a code example
Assistant> Sure! Here's a simple closure example...

You> exit

Type exit or quit to end the session.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Requires a running vllama run_llm server
  • Conversation context is maintained for the full session
  • The VS Code extension uses the same server — both can connect simultaneously

docs.title: VS Code Integration
docs.text: The Vllama VS Code extension connects to the same localhost:2513 server. See the Local LLM in VS Code guide for the full setup walkthrough.

docs.title: Model Recommendations
docs.text: Use Case Recommended Model Size Code generation Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct ~1GB General chat microsoft/DialoGPT-medium ~1.5GB Capable general meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf ~14GB (gated) Low-spec machine Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct ~1GB

docs.title: Speech Commands
docs.text: Text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and text translation — all running locally.

docs.title: vllama tts — Text to Speech
docs.text: Convert text to speech using a local TTS engine. Audio plays through your system speakers.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama tts [--text <text>]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Speak a string directly
vllama tts --text "Hello from Vllama. This is a test."

# Interactive mode — enter text at the prompt
vllama tts
# Enter text: Hello world

docs.title: vllama stt — Speech to Text
docs.text: Transcribe speech from your microphone or an audio file using Google Speech Recognition.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama stt [--path <audio_file>] [--language <lang_code>]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --path microphone Path to an audio file to transcribe --language en-US Language code for recognition

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Transcribe from microphone
vllama stt
# Output: Listening... Speak now!
# Output: Transcribed: Hello world

# Transcribe from file
vllama stt --path recording.wav

# Specify language
vllama stt --language hi-IN   # Hindi
vllama stt --language te-IN   # Telugu

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Microphone input requires a working audio input device
  • Uses Google Speech Recognition under the hood — requires internet for the actual transcription
  • --path supports WAV and other common audio formats

docs.title: vllama translate — Text Translation
docs.text: Translate text between languages using a local NLLB (No Language Left Behind) model from Meta. Runs entirely offline after the first model download.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama translate --text <text> [--src <lang>] [--tgt <lang>] [--model <model_id>]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Short Default Description --text required Text to translate --src en Source language code --tgt fr Target language code --model NLLB default HuggingFace model ID to use

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# English to French
vllama translate --text "Hello, how are you?" --src en --tgt fr

# French to English
vllama translate --text "Bonjour le monde" --src fr --tgt en

# English to Hindi
vllama translate --text "Good morning" --src en --tgt hi

# English to Telugu
vllama translate --text "Welcome to Vllama" --src en --tgt te

docs.title: Language Codes
docs.text:
NLLB uses BCP-47 style codes. Common ones:

Language Code English en Hindi hi Telugu te Tamil ta French fr Spanish es German de Chinese (Simplified) zh Arabic ar Portuguese pt

For the full list, refer to the NLLB language list.

docs.title: vllama train — AutoML Training
docs.text: Automatically trains and compares multiple ML models on preprocessed data with hyperparameter tuning, and produces a ranked leaderboard.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama train --path <data_folder> --target <column>

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Short Description --path -p Path to folder containing train_data.csv and test_data.csv (output from vllama data) --target -t Name of the target column

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
1. Auto-detects task type — classification or regression based on the target column
  2. Trains all models with RandomizedSearchCV hyperparameter tuning on each
  3. Evaluates every model on the test set with comprehensive metrics
  4. Ranks models in a leaderboard
  5. Saves all models and generates visualizations
  6. Produces an HTML report with all results

docs.title: Models Trained
docs.text:
ClassificationRegression
  • Logistic Regression
  • Random Forest
  • XGBoost
  • LightGBM
  • CatBoost
  • SVM
  • KNN
  • MLP (Neural Net)
  • Naive Bayes
  • Random Forest
  • XGBoost
  • LightGBM
  • CatBoost
  • SVR
  • KNN
  • MLP (Neural Net)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Standard usage after vllama data
vllama train --path ./output_folder_20240101_120000 --target price

# Short form
vllama train -p ./output_folder_20240101_120000 -t label

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text:
results/
├── model_summary.csv           ← Leaderboard: all models ranked by metric
├── best_model.pkl              ← Best model, loadable with joblib
├── best_model.txt              ← Best model name and score
├── report.html                 ← Full interactive HTML report ← open this
└── per_model/
    ├── RandomForest/
    │   ├── RandomForest_best_model.pkl
    │   ├── RandomForest_tuning_results.csv
    │   ├── RandomForest_confusion_matrix.png  (classification)
    │   └── RandomForest_roc_curve.png         (binary classification)
    ├── XGBoost/
    │   └── ...
    └── ...

Open report.html

After training, open results/report.html in your browser. It contains the full leaderboard, per-model metrics, and all visualizations in one place.

docs.title: Loading the Best Model
docs.text:
import joblib

model = joblib.load("results/best_model.pkl")
predictions = model.predict(X_test)

docs.title: Full Pipeline
docs.text:
vllama data --path raw_data.csv --target price
vllama train --path ./output_folder_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS --target price
# Open results/report.html

See the AutoML Pipeline Guide for a detailed walkthrough with a real dataset.

docs.title: vllama run_video — Video Generation
docs.text: Generate short videos from text prompts using text-to-video models.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama run_video <model_name> [--prompt <text>] [--service <service>] [--output_dir <dir>]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Short Default Description model_name required HuggingFace model ID --prompt -p interactive Text prompt for generation --service -s local Cloud service (kaggle) --output_dir -o current dir Where to save the output video

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Generate video locally
vllama run_video damo-vilab/text-to-video-ms-1.7b --prompt "A cat playing piano"

# Interactive mode
vllama run_video damo-vilab/text-to-video-ms-1.7b
# Prompt> A sunset over the ocean
# Prompt> exit

# Offload to Kaggle GPU (recommended — video gen is VRAM-heavy)
vllama run_video damo-vilab/text-to-video-ms-1.7b --service kaggle --prompt "A robot dancing"

# Custom output folder
vllama run_video damo-vilab/text-to-video-ms-1.7b -p "Waves crashing on shore" -o ./videos

docs.title: Recommended Model
docs.text: Model Description damo-vilab/text-to-video-ms-1.7b ModelScope's 1.7B text-to-video model — solid quality for short clips

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Video generation is VRAM-heavy

Text-to-video models typically need 8GB+ VRAM for comfortable local use. If you have less, use --service kaggle to offload to Kaggle's free T4 GPU.

Output videos are saved as .mp4 files in the specified output directory.

docs.title: vllama view3d — 3D Model Viewer
docs.text: Open and interactively view 3D model files in a local viewer window.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: vllama view3d --path <model_file>

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text: Format Extension Polygon File Format .ply GL Transmission Format .glb / .gltf Wavefront OBJ .obj Stereolithography .stl Filmbox .fbx

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
vllama view3d --path model.ply
vllama view3d --path scan.glb
vllama view3d --path object.obj

docs.title: Common Workflow
docs.text:
# Step 1: Generate a 3D model from an image on Kaggle GPU
vllama image3d --path photo.jpg --service kaggle -o ./3d_outputs

# Step 2: View the result
vllama view3d --path ./3d_outputs/output.ply

The viewer opens in a native window with mouse controls for rotating, zooming, and panning the model.

docs.title: Image Generation Commands
docs.text: Commands for running diffusion models to generate images, managing downloaded models, and interacting with running model sessions.

docs.text: Run a diffusion model to generate images from text prompts.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Short Default Description model_name required HuggingFace model ID --prompt -p interactive Text prompt for generation --service -s local Cloud service to offload to (kaggle) --output_dir -o current dir Where to save generated images

# Generate locally (requires GPU or patience on CPU)
vllama run stabilityai/sd-turbo --prompt "A futuristic cityscape at dusk"

# Interactive mode — enter multiple prompts
vllama run stabilityai/sd-turbo

# Prompt> exit

docs.text:
Images are saved as:

  • vllama_output_<timestamp>.png — local generation
  • vllama_kaggle_<timestamp>.png — Kaggle generation

docs.title: GPU Optimization
docs.text:
Vllama automatically adjusts settings based on your hardware:

Hardware Precision Resolution Notes GPU > 3GB VRAM float16 512×512 Full quality GPU ≤ 3GB VRAM float32 Reduced steps Memory-efficient attention enabled CPU float32 Reduced steps Works but slow

No GPU? Use Kaggle

Add --service kaggle to any vllama run command to run on Kaggle's free T4 GPU. See the No GPU Guide.

docs.title: vllama show models — List Supported Models
docs.text:
vllama show models

Lists all vision models supported by Vllama with descriptions.

docs.title: vllama install — Download a Model
docs.text:
Pre-download a model's weights to local cache so the first run is instant:

vllama install stabilityai/sd-turbo
vllama install CompVis/stable-diffusion-v1-4

Model weights are cached in ~/.cache/huggingface.

docs.title: vllama list — List Downloaded Models
docs.text:
vllama list models

Shows all models currently cached on your machine.

docs.title: vllama uninstall — Remove a Model
docs.text:
vllama uninstall stabilityai/sd-turbo

Removes the model from local cache to free disk space.

docs.title: vllama post — Send a Prompt to a Running Session
docs.text:
If you have a model session already running in the background, send a prompt without entering interactive mode:

vllama post "A waterfall in a rainforest" --output_dir ./outputs

docs.title: vllama stop — Stop a Running Session
docs.text:
vllama stop

Stops the currently running model session and frees GPU memory.

docs.title: Full AutoML Pipeline Guide
docs.text: A complete walkthrough: from a raw CSV to a trained, saved model — using only Vllama.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
raw_data.csv
     ↓
vllama data     → cleaned data + visualizations
     ↓
vllama train    → 9 trained models + leaderboard + best_model.pkl
     ↓
results/report.html

docs.title: Example Dataset
docs.text:
We'll use the classic Titanic survival dataset to demonstrate.

# Download the dataset
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datasciencedojo/datasets/master/titanic.csv

docs.title: Step 1: Preprocess the Data
docs.text:
vllama data --path titanic.csv --target Survived --test_size 0.2

What Vllama does automatically:

  • Detects Survived is a binary classification target
  • Drops irrelevant columns (Name, Ticket, Cabin)
  • Fills missing Age values using KNN imputation
  • Encodes Sex and Embarked as numeric features
  • Scales numeric features
  • Splits into 80% train / 20% test

After it finishes, you'll see something like:

✓ Loaded dataset: 891 rows × 12 columns
✓ Removed duplicates: 0
✓ Handled missing values: Age (177), Cabin (687), Embarked (2)
✓ Encoded categoricals: Sex, Embarked
✓ Scaled features: Age, Fare, SibSp, Parch
✓ Feature selection: removed 2 low-variance features
✓ Saved train/test split to: output_folder_20240101_120000/

docs.title: Step 2: Train All Models
docs.text:
# Use the folder name printed in Step 1
vllama train --path ./output_folder_20240101_120000 --target Survived

Vllama trains all 9 classification models (each with hyperparameter tuning via RandomizedSearchCV):

  • Logistic Regression
  • Random Forest
  • XGBoost
  • LightGBM
  • CatBoost
  • SVM
  • KNN
  • MLP
  • Naive Bayes

This takes a few minutes depending on your machine.

docs.title: Step 3: Review Results
docs.text:
Open the generated report:

# macOS
open results/report.html

# Linux
xdg-open results/report.html

# Windows
start results/report.html

The report contains:

  • Leaderboard — all models ranked by accuracy / F1
  • Per-model metrics — precision, recall, AUC, confusion matrices
  • Best model — highlighted at the top

You can also check the leaderboard in the terminal:

cat results/model_summary.csv

docs.title: Step 4: Use the Best Model
docs.text:
import joblib
import pandas as pd

# Load the best model
model = joblib.load("results/best_model.pkl")

# Predict on new data
new_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "Pclass": [3], "Sex": [1], "Age": [22],
    "SibSp": [1], "Parch": [0], "Fare": [7.25]
})
prediction = model.predict(new_data)
print("Survived:", prediction[0])

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
On a small dataset (< 1000 rows)? Training finishes in under a minute. Larger datasets (50k+ rows) may take 10–20 minutes due to hyperparameter search.

Getting a bad best model score? Check the visualizations in output_folder_*/visualizations/ — the correlation matrix and mutual information plots can tell you if features are informative.

Want to reproduce the preprocessing later? transformation_metadata.json in the output folder stores all encoders and scalers. You can load them to preprocess new inference data the same way.

docs.title: Local LLM in VS Code
docs.text: Use Vllama to chat with a local language model directly inside VS Code's native chat panel — no API keys, no subscriptions, no data sent to the cloud.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Vllama runs a local LLM as an HTTP server on your machine. The Vllama VS Code extension connects to that server and plugs it into VS Code's native Chat with AI panel. Your model, your hardware, your data.

Your Machine
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  vllama run_llm (Flask server :2513)        │
│         ↕  HTTP                             │
│  VS Code Vllama Extension                  │
│         ↕  VS Code Chat API                 │
│  VS Code Chat panel                         │
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Step 1: Install the VS Code Extension
docs.text:
1. Open VS Code
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+X (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+X (macOS)
  3. Search for Vllama
  4. Click Install
  5. Reload VS Code when prompted

docs.title: Step 2: Start the Local LLM Server
docs.text:
In your terminal:

vllama run_llm Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct

On first run, this downloads the model weights (~1GB for Qwen 0.5B). Wait for:

* Running on http://localhost:2513

Keep this terminal open — closing it stops the server.

docs.title: Step 3: Chat in VS Code
docs.text:
1. In VS Code, open the Chat panel: View → Chat with AI (or Ctrl+Alt+I)
  2. Select your Vllama local model from the model dropdown
  3. Start chatting

docs.title: Recommended Models by Use Case
docs.text: Goal Model Download Size Code help, fast Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct ~1 GB General assistant (low RAM) microsoft/DialoGPT-medium ~1.5 GB Better quality (needs 8GB+ RAM) meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf ~14 GB

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"VS Code extension can't connect"

  • Make sure vllama run_llm is running and shows Running on http://localhost:2513
  • Check VS Code extension settings — the default port is 2513
  • On Linux, check if a firewall is blocking localhost connections: sudo ufw status

Model responses are slow

Smaller models (0.5B–1B parameters) respond in seconds even on CPU. Larger models (7B+) need a GPU or are slow on CPU. Try Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct for fast responses.

"Model not found"

Verify the model ID is valid on huggingface.co. Gated models (Llama 2) require a HuggingFace token:

export HF_TOKEN=your_huggingface_token
vllama run_llm meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf

docs.title: Also: Chat from the Terminal
docs.text:
You don't need VS Code — you can also chat directly from a second terminal window:

# Terminal 2 (while server is running in Terminal 1)
vllama chat_llm

Both the CLI chat and VS Code extension can connect to the same server simultaneously.

docs.title: Run Heavy AI Models for Free — No GPU Needed
docs.text:
Vllama has a built-in bridge to Kaggle's free GPU (NVIDIA T4, ~16GB VRAM). You submit a task from your laptop, it runs on Kaggle's infrastructure, and the output downloads back to your machine automatically.

This means you can run Stable Diffusion, text-to-video models, and 3D reconstruction — even on a 4GB RAM laptop — for free.

docs.title: What You Need
docs.text:
• A Kaggle account (free, takes 2 minutes)
  • Phone number for verification (Kaggle requires this for GPU access)
  • Vllama installed: pip install vllama

docs.title: Step 1: Get Your Kaggle API Key
docs.text:
1. Log in at kaggle.com
  2. Click your profile icon (top right) → Settings
  3. Scroll to the API section
  4. Click Create New Token — this downloads kaggle.json

Open the file. It looks like:

{
  "username": "yourname",
  "key": "abc123yourkeyhere"
}

docs.title: Step 2: Connect Vllama to Kaggle
docs.text:
vllama login --service kaggle --username yourname --key abc123yourkeyhere

If your kaggle.json is already at ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json (default Kaggle CLI location), just run:

vllama login --service kaggle

docs.title: Step 3: Run Something
docs.text: Now just add --service kaggle to any supported command.

docs.title: Generate an Image
docs.text:
vllama run stabilityai/sd-turbo --service kaggle --prompt "A cyberpunk street at night, neon lights, rain"

Vllama will: 1. Create a Kaggle kernel with GPU 2. Install dependencies 3. Run the model 4. Download vllama_kaggle_<timestamp>.png to your current directory

Takes about 3–5 minutes total. The actual generation is under 10 seconds on the T4.

docs.title: Generate a Video
docs.text: vllama run_video damo-vilab/text-to-video-ms-1.7b --service kaggle --prompt "A sunset over the ocean, cinematic"

docs.title: Generate a 3D Model from an Image
docs.text: vllama image3d --path my_object.jpg --service kaggle -o ./3d_output

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"Kaggle API credentials not found"

vllama login --service kaggle --username YOUR_USERNAME --key YOUR_KEY

"GPU quota exceeded"

Kaggle gives ~30 GPU hours/week for free accounts. If you hit the limit, wait until your quota resets (weekly), or check quota at kaggle.com/account.

Kernel takes too long / times out

Kaggle notebooks have a 12-hour session limit. Individual inference tasks take 3–10 minutes, well within this.

First run is slow

The first run installs dependencies inside the Kaggle kernel. Subsequent runs reuse the environment and are faster.

docs.title: Kaggle GPU Limits (Free Tier)
docs.text:
Resource Limit GPU type NVIDIA T4 (16GB VRAM) Weekly GPU hours ~30 hours Session max duration 12 hours Disk space 73GB Internet Enabled

For most use cases — generating images, videos, 3D models — you'll stay well within the weekly quota.
